name: Monzombo
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog monz1249 lists only classification refs (Bennett 1983; Boyd & Pasch 1988); no grammar/phonology located online

new_statements.quote: Accent tonique. — L'accent tonique consiste dans un ‘ coup de voix ’ sans élévation sensible du ton. La syllabe qui le porte est prononcée avec plus d'intensité ou d'effort. Il se trouve ordinairement sur la première syllabe non affectée du signe de brièveté. Accent de hauteur. — L'accent de hauteur consiste dans une élévation du ton, soit sur un mot monosyllabique, soit sur une ou plusieurs syllabes du même mot. Il est indiqué par un accent aigu placé sur la syllabe accentuée. Remarque. — Le n° 1 désigne le Gmbwaga, le n° 2 le Gbanziri, le n° 3 le Mônjômbo.
new_statements.translation: Tonic accent. — The tonic accent consists of a 'stroke of the voice' without any perceptible rise in pitch. The syllable that carries it is pronounced with more intensity or effort. It is ordinarily found on the first syllable not marked with the sign of shortness. Pitch accent. — The pitch accent consists of a rise in tone, either on a monosyllabic word or on one or more syllables of the same word. It is indicated by an acute accent placed on the accented syllable. Note. — No. 1 designates Gmbwaga, no. 2 Gbanziri, no. 3 Monjombo.
new_statements.citation: Calloc'h, J. 1911. Vocabulaire français-gmbwaga-gbanziri-monjombo (Congo français), précédé d'éléments de grammaire. Paris: Librairie Paul Geuthner.
new_statements.locator: Éléments de grammaire, p. 8, paragraphs 'Accentuation', 'Accent tonique', 'Accent de hauteur' (PDF page 12; running head 'GRAMMAIRE GMBWAGA-GBANZIRI-MONJOMBO 8')
new_statements.rule_in_words: Intensity stress ('accent tonique') normally falls on the first syllable of the word that is not marked short (breve); pitch ('accent de hauteur', i.e. tone) is a separate, independently marked property that can sit on any syllable(s). The statement is made jointly for Gmbwaga (Ngbaka Ma'bo), Gbanziri and Monjombo (Monzombo), treated by the author as three dialects of one language.
new_statements.exceptions: 'ordinairement' (ordinarily); a syllable marked short (signe de brièveté) is skipped, so stress moves rightward off short initial syllables. No examples given. Modern sources (Peeters blurb for Bouquiaux & Thomas 2018) describe Monzombo as a four-level tone language, and Moñino 1995:285 says of the neighbouring Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka group that none of those languages shows accent, intensity or length phenomena, so the 1911 intensity-stress claim is unconfirmed by later work.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (isolated citation forms in a missionary vocabulary). Caution: the accentuation paragraph is an authorial template that Calloc'h reused word-for-word in his 1911 Vocabulaire français-gbéa (where the position word is 'pénultième'), so only the position word is language-specific and the 'non affectée du signe de brièveté' clause is boilerplate. No Monzombo-specific examples of stress placement are given.
new_statements.identity_note: Calloc'h 1911 calls the variety 'Monjombo' (also 'Mônjômbo'), one of three 'dialectes d'une même langue' with Gmbwaga (= Ngbaka Ma'bo, ngba1284) and Gbanziri (gban1258), spoken on the Ubangi in then-French Congo; Glottolog maps it to monz1249 / ISO moj. The stress statement is made jointly for all three languages, not for Monzombo alone. The 2018 Peeters dictionary describes Monzombo of the Ubangi/Congo river banks (CAR and both Congos), which is the same language.

sources.locator: Éléments de grammaire, p. 8, paragraphs 'Accentuation', 'Accent tonique', 'Accent de hauteur' (PDF page 12; running head 'GRAMMAIRE GMBWAGA-GBANZIRI-MONJOMBO 8')
sources.note: Joint statement for Gmbwaga (= Ngbaka Ma'bo), Gbanziri and Monjombo (= Monzombo), which the Introduction calls 'trois dialectes d'une même langue': the accent tonique ('coup de voix' without pitch rise, more intensity/effort) 'se trouve ordinairement sur la première syllabe non affectée du signe de brièveté'; separately an accent de hauteur (pitch) on one or more syllables, marked by acute accent. The paragraph is a template the author reused verbatim in his 1911 Gbéa vocabulary with only the position word changed (pénultième there).
